brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A sweet leaf tea from the ridges of Jinyun Mountain in Beibei, Chongqing, made not from the tea plant but from a tree of the beech family with purplish young leaves.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Yearly output is put at only a few thousand kilograms. Local accounts say it was shown at a Paris exposition in 1937 and that Zhu De drank several bowls on a visit in spring 1956; a legend about the source of its sweetness also circulates. Little more is documented.
processing: Young leaves and shoots are steamed, fried and dried.
taste_profile: Fresh and mellow, with a sweetness that lingers long after drinking.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
